title: Wendell and the Garden
premise: Hazel Coldharbour, a hedge-witch's runaway apprentice, has spent seven years selling small charms in the city of Vell, where magic is outlawed and her old life is a death sentence. When a blind date named Wendell Ash turns out to be the figure foretold in a century-old book of prophecies, both are pulled through a tear in reality into the Sundered Garden — the withered borderland between the mortal realm and the fae Otherworld. To survive, they must reforge the broken covenant that once kept the realms in balance, a task that forces Hazel to confront the mentor she betrayed and Wendell to accept that he is not entirely human. As the garden's dying magic corrupts everyone who draws on it, Hazel must choose between sealing the covenant with her own name erased from existence or letting both realms fall; she chooses sacrifice, but Wendell's love — and his hidden nature as the garden's last living seed — restores what she gave up, at the cost of his mortality.
about_author: Emrys Halloran is the pen name of a former botanist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered plants before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy rooted in folklore, gardens, and the quiet violence of duty, and live somewhere damp with too many houseplants.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In rain-soaked Vell, Hazel sells a luck-charm to a nervous clerk while dodging a Wardens' sweep, establishing her careful double life and the guilt she carries about abandoning her mentor. Emotional beat: weary self-sufficiency masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Table for Two
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her landlady strong-arms her into a blind date at a canal-side teahouse. She meets Wendell Ash, a gentle, awkward mapmaker who notices things he shouldn't. Their conversation is unexpectedly easy. Emotional beat: cautious hope, the first warmth in seven years.

chapters.title: The Book That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confesses he found an unlisted book in the archive where he works: a prophecy naming 'the ash-born' and 'the runaway of the cold harbour' meeting tonight. He thought it was a joke. Emotional beat: vulnerability, the terror of being believed.

chapters.title: Ink Moves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As they argue over the absurdity, the prophecy's ink begins to crawl, rewriting itself around their names. The teahouse gutters out like a candle. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as choice becomes fate.

chapters.title: Through the Hedge
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A tear opens and pulls them into the Sundered Garden — a vast, half-dead borderland of petrified orchards and grey rivers. They are found by Briarlock, a fox-headed herald who has waited a century for them. Emotional beat: disorientation and reluctant awe.

chapters.title: Rules of the Withered Ground
chapters.summary: Briarlock's exposition via Hazel's POV. The covenant between realms was sealed by three oaths; one oath-keeper died, one vanished, and the third went mad. Without renewal by the next dark moon, both realms unravel. Emotional beat: the weight of an inheritance neither asked for.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Taught Me
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn why she fled her apprenticeship under Mother Yew: she used forbidden magic to save a child and let her mentor take the blame. Emotional beat: shame that has calcified into identity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Casts No Shadow
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the garden, Wendell casts no shadow and flowers bloom where he sleeps. Briarlock watches him with reverence and fear. Wendell begins to suspect he isn't fully mortal. Emotional beat: uncanny self-alienation.

chapters.title: First Oath: The Well of Names
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The first oath requires a true name freely given at the Well of Names. Hazel refuses to give hers — names have power, and hers is all she has left. Wendell gives his instead. Emotional beat: trust tested by old wounds.

chapters.title: The Toll
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Giving his name costs Wendell his memories of Vell — including the date, the teahouse, the beginning of them. Hazel realizes what he paid only after. Emotional beat: grief for something barely begun.

chapters.title: Thieves of the Orchard
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They're ambushed by the Hollowed — humans who drew on the garden's corrupted magic and became fruit-stealing wraiths. Hazel uses hedge-craft to drive them off, revealing skills she'd sworn away. Emotional beat: the thrill and danger of reclaiming power.

chapters.title: Mother Yew Lives
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Among the Hollowed's captives, Hazel finds Mother Yew — aged, half-mad, but alive, imprisoned for a century as the vanished second oath-keeper. Her mentor's greeting is not forgiveness but a slap. Emotional beat: reckoning long deferred.

chapters.title: The Mad Gardener
chapters.summary: Mother Yew's fragmented POV. She reveals the third oath-keeper: the Gardener, who went mad tending the covenant alone and now prunes anything that grows too close to truth. She agrees to help — if Hazel kneels and finishes her apprenticeship. Emotional beat: pride versus necessity.

chapters.title: Lessons in the Dark
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Reluctant apprenticeship scenes: Hazel relearns magic properly, discovering how much she'd warped by working alone. Meanwhile Wendell tends the garden and it blooms for him unnaturally fast. Emotional beat: humility, slow repair.

chapters.title: Second Oath: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The second oath lies in a chapel sunk beneath the grey river, guarded by a drowned choir. Wendell nearly drowns; Hazel breaks her vow of caution and burns years of hoarded charm-magic to save him. Emotional beat: love confessed mid-crisis.

chapters.title: What I Would Give
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude, alternating POV. Recovering in a dry alcove, Hazel and Wendell finally speak plainly — about the prophecy, the price already paid, the price still coming. They choose each other knowing the covenant may demand more. Emotional beat: tenderness under sentence.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Shears
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Gardener finds them, serene and terrible, pruning a grove of screaming topiary. He recognizes Wendell instantly — and calls him 'seedling.' Emotional beat: dread; the story's central mystery cracks open.

chapters.title: Seedling
chapters.summary: Mother Yew's POV. Truth revealed: Wendell is the last seed of the World-Tree, raised human in Vell to hide him from the Gardener, who wants to plant him — which would renew the covenant but erase Wendell as a person. Emotional beat: horror of being a means, not a man.

chapters.title: Runaways Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel proposes fleeing: let the realms fray slowly, live out their lives in the margins. Wendell refuses — he's seen the Hollowed up close. First real fight between them. Emotional beat: love against duty, both sides right.

chapters.title: The City Fraying
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, vision. Touching the garden's roots, Wendell sees Vell unraveling: canals running backwards, Wardens' anti-magic wards becoming cages, people forgetting each other. Emotional beat: the abstract stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Choir
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. To reach the final oath-site, Hazel bargains with the drowned choir, trading memories of her mother. Mother Yew protests; Hazel has learned that payment given freely is the whole of the law. Emotional beat: costly growth — she pays without bitterness now.

chapters.title: The Third Gate
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They arrive at the Heartwood Gate, where the covenant was first sworn. It will open only for three oath-keepers. They are two, plus a madwoman. Emotional beat: the summit in sight, the party incomplete.

chapters.title: Mother Yew's Confession
chapters.summary: Mother Yew's POV. She admits she didn't take Hazel's blame nobly — she took it to bind Hazel to her forever, a leash disguised as sacrifice. Her madness began when the leash failed. Emotional beat: the mentor unmasked; pity replaces awe.

chapters.title: Forgiveness Is Not a Debt
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel forgives Mother Yew anyway — not because she deserves it, but because carrying the grudge is the last thing tying Hazel to her old self. Something in the garden responds: green shoots. Emotional beat: liberation through release.

chapters.title: The Gardener Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Gardener corners them: give me the seedling willingly and I'll spare your city, your mentor, your love. He shows Wendell a vision of the peace that planting would buy. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Hazel Says No
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel counters with her own plan: she'll give her name to the covenant instead, erasing herself so the garden can root in her emptied self rather than in Wendell. Mother Yew calls it suicide; Hazel calls it the lesson finally learned. Emotional beat: resolve sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Gate
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Wendell refuses to be saved by her erasure; Hazel refuses to be a widow to a tree. Briarlock, quietly, points out the covenant never said whose name — only that it be given in love. Emotional beat: the riddle's hinge, hope rekindled.

chapters.title: A Name Given in Love
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The solution: not one name but an exchange — each gives their name to the other, so the covenant takes hold of a bond rather than a person. But no one knows if it will work, and the dark moon rises tonight. Emotional beat: leap of faith.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Last Pruning
chapters.summary: Climax begins, both POVs. As they attempt the exchange at the Heartwood Gate, the Gardener attacks, determined that order require a single sacrifice. Mother Yew holds the gate's threshold at terrible cost. Emotional beat: desperate, blazing resistance.

chapters.title: What the Tree Remembers
chapters.summary: Climax, Wendell's POV. Mid-ritual, Wendell touches the World-Tree's memory and learns the Gardener was the first oath-keeper, driven mad by giving everything alone — the fate Hazel almost chose. Emotional beat: compassion for the enemy; the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Climax, both POVs. Hazel and Wendell speak each other's names into the covenant. The garden floods with light; the Gardener, offered a share in the bond rather than dominion, hesitates — and Mother Yew's sacrifice tips him into surrender. Emotional beat: transcendence through mutual giving.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Green
chapters.summary: Falling action, Hazel's POV. The Sundered Garden blooms; the grey river runs clear; the Hollowed begin to wake. But Wendell is fading — the seed in him spent. Emotional beat: joy shadowed by imminent loss.

chapters.title: The Last Seed
chapters.summary: Falling action, Wendell's POV. Wendell chooses to remain in the garden as its keeper, mortal now, tethered to the borderland rather than either realm. Hazel can visit through the hedge but not stay. Emotional beat: bittersweet bargain accepted with open eyes.

chapters.title: Mother Yew's Retirement
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Mother Yew, freed of her century of duty, chooses to stay in the garden as its teacher, taking on the waking Hollowed as students. She and Hazel part as equals. Emotional beat: reconciliation completed, gently.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel returns to Vell, where the fraying has healed and magic is no longer outlawed — the new covenant made openness possible. She reopens her charm stall openly, under her own name. Emotional beat: coming home to oneself.

chapters.title: The Mapmaker's Letters
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter, both POVs. Letters pass through the hedge: Wendell mapping the garden's regrowth, Hazel describing a city learning magic again. Their love persists across the boundary, changed but real. Emotional beat: longing transmuted into devotion.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the spring equinox, Hazel walks through the hedge for their allotted day together. The garden has grown a small cottage from the World-Tree's fallen branch. Emotional beat: earned peace, savored.

chapters.title: The New Apprentice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A Vell street-kid with wild talent follows Hazel through the hedge and asks to learn. Hazel, remembering her own flight, says yes — and brings her to Mother Yew and Wendell. Emotional beat: the cycle repaired, legacy chosen rather than imposed.

chapters.title: Wendell and the Garden
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV closing on Wendell. One year on: the covenant holds, the prophecy book in Vell's archive now ends with two names intertwined rather than sacrificed. Wendell plants a seed that will grow into a door that never closes. Emotional beat: quiet, durable hope — love and duty reconciled.
